newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore banking system makes first Internet sale.
newsitem.headline: Singapore banking system makes first Internet sale.

text.p: Singapore's bank payment clearing system, the Network for Electronic Transfers (S) Pte Ltd (NETS), completed its first live transaction via a new Internet payment system on Monday.

Credit card company Visa International said the transaction involved electronic versions of Visa and its rival Mastercard issued by two local banks making purchases from Internet shopping malls in Singapore.
NETS, which groups DBS, OCBC, OUB, UOB, Keppel and Tat Lee banks, launched its Internet pilot project in April.
Several thousand credit card users in Singapore were expected to be involved in trials making secure purchases from a wide range of local merchants by August, Visa said.
Industry estimates predict Internet commerce will grow by more than 300 percent a year in the Asia/Pacific region over the next five years.
Total Internet trade is expected to reach $2.2 billion in the region by 2000, compared with about US$6.7 million in 1995.
